text:
Maya Chen: Quick sync — GlacierBank legal signed a clause: all inference for their org must route to their private model endpoint in us-west-2 (air-gapped tenant). They want this enforced at the gateway level so even accidental host selection doesn't leak. Is this something we can ship as an "org override" rule?
Alex R: We can. Two quick questions: 1) should it be header-based (X-Redwood-Org-Route) or token-bound? 2) need fallback behavior if private capacity is down?
Maya Chen: Prefer token-bound + header as belt-and-suspenders. Fallback: fail closed (deny) for now — contract says no fallback to shared models.
Rohit S: Security note: failing closed affects availability; ops should approve. Also we must add an allowlist so only GlacierBank's reserved tokens can trigger the override.
Priya K: From console/UX POV we need: visible active overrides, who approved, and an expiry/TTL. Also a way to audit every routed request (route decision, model id, capacity stub). We should avoid hidden toggles.
Alex R: Agreed. Implementation sketch (gateway rule):
```json
{"match": {"org_id": "glacierbank"}, "action": {"route_to": "private://glacierbank-usw2/model-v2", "require_token_allowlist": ["glacierbank-token-*"], "on_unavailable": "deny"}}
```
Rohit S: Implementation concerns: 1) where do we store these customer allowlists? 2) must be encrypted and auditable. 3) rotation of tokens should be supported (wildcards ok but prefer explicit entries).
Priya K: Console page should show the matching predicate (org_id/header), the effective action (route_to), last evaluated timestamp, and a link to the approval ticket. Also add a quick revoke button for SRE.
Maya Chen: Ops/CM: can we require two approvers for high-risk overrides? GlacierBank flagged as high-risk sensitive.
Alex R: We can add an "approval_level" flag: normal vs high-risk (requires 2 approvers). We'll wire that into the rollout workflow.
Rohit S: Telemetry: emit a decision event per request: {org_id, rule_id, model_variant, routed=true/false, reason}. Add a sampling for raw request bodies. Also tag in traces.
Priya K: UX question: show an expected cost delta when routing to private (est monthly uplift) so sales/customer success can sign off.
Maya Chen: Good call — finance already provided a per-token uplift estimate. Add that to the approval modal.
Alex R: Who owns the CIDR/GW firewall changes? GlacierBank's infra team needs a one-time peering. I can take the infra ticket.
Priya K: I'll prototype a console mockup (approve/revoke/audit) and link the mock in the ticket.
Rohit S: Security wants an automated audit log push to their SIEM via our log-forwarder; ticket #SEC-783.
console-bot: Created RFC rfc/2025-org-overrides and attached draft: https://redwood.internal/rfc/2025
Maya Chen: Action items: Alex - implement gateway predicate + allowlist + deny fallback; Rohit - hook audit events & SIEM forwarder; Priya - console mock + approval flow; security - SEC-783 follow-up. I'll open a delivery PR once RFC is updated.
Alex R: I'll aim for a prototype in the gateway branch by EOW.
Rohit S: Noted. If we hit capacity issues we need an auto-escalation to dedicated-ops paging.
Priya K: Also surface the override in per-org dashboard and per-route latency/cost charts.
Maya Chen: Thanks everyone :thumbsup: I'll post the formal request to the approvals channel and attach the contract clause.
Alex R: One more: let's add a short TTL (30d) by default so overrides expire unless renewed. Prevents stale permanent exceptions.
Maya Chen: Yep. 30d default, with option for 1y renewal for enterprise.
Priya K: Mock and notes: https://redwood.internal/console/prototypes/glacierbank-override (will update)
